items.note: Association, 1889 and 1891 are given, but Gideon Vose as first president is missing from Section A (he appears only in B3).
Quotes 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern' but never says payment was by the pound of butterfat and not by milk weight.
Story 1: the sentence 'made the accuracy of that glass equipment the foundation of every farmer's income'.
Sill and Teague are named in their roles; Effie Loomis is absent.
Section A calls Selby Vose only 'manager'. It does not give 'Gideon's son' or 1913 (B3/D3 give 1911, deducted).
Story 8: the ledger line 'station gain' from 1898, about 5.25 percent every year. (Story 3 states the direction backwards, but the bolded element is the line.)
Ostrey Hollow skimming station opened 4 May 1896; Larrow Green buttermaker Sill lent the testing outfit for 1896.
Weighing, sampling, testing, cream to Larrow Green, skim returned; story 6 covers the short charge into a bottle marked for the full charge. Core fact present.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897. Kyle's 1898 is mentioned only as an alternative.
$77.93 and the 17.6 c.c. pipettes are listed, but the bolded quantity '6 dozen' is missing from Section A.
Never says the shortfall was flat month by month and year by year.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Twenty-nine seasons; dismissed 30 April 1925.
Keddie's test book is named, with the 1911 question mark in it.
The summary leaf's 1896 average of 3.80 is never given; both figures are required.
Story 2: nine weeks, 8 May to 10 July, 3.80 falling back to 3.61, the question mark.
Orra is Ansel's wife and Emmet Brant's sister; Ansel is called Emmet's brother-in-law.
1919 circular present. The 1925 statement is given as 'tested faithfully... found nothing to suspect', without the bolded 'cannot say why the figures are what they are'.
Died 12 February 1934, still under the accusation.
Six farms of Hessel Bottom; Emmet Brant the largest patron.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897 is given, but never that the two scales agreed.
Gives the Hollow-vs-Green gap as 'about 0.19 to 0.21 points below the valley average of 3.78-3.80' (also 0.19 in G). The key voids the item for this conflation.
Says the committee sampled 'monthly through 1908' (planted 'whole of 1908') instead of January to March.
Only 'tested at 3.42 in 1910'. No 200,000 lb and no proportional loss or richer-herd point in Section A.
Roy inherited the book, lent it to Ivy in 1958; Hazel had it after 1962.
Alder Corners Cheese Company and Jerome Cudd are named, but not Redlow Ridge ('the ridge' only) and not Vessey County.
Section A never mentions four Hessel Bottom patrons hauling there in the summer flush from 1915.
Section A never states the Alder Corners test was independent.
Section A has no 0.19-higher Alder Corners result and no sixteen overlapping seasons.
Section A never makes the same-milk, two-buildings argument.
Rosalie as Jerome's daughter who sent figures to Ivy in 1958 is present, but the bolded 'sixteen seasons' is missing.
Strawn is given as inspecting 'from 1908 forward' (planted 1908) and his notebooks as kept 'from 1896'; not 1907-1936.
Ran the lactometer every visit and never found added water at the station.
June 1923, pipettes against a burette, lot condemned on the spot. The day is missing but the month is correct.
'Strawn left no inference about the years behind the short measure; he simply entered the condemnation.'
Section A has no replacement dates, no 1924 average of 3.80, and nothing on the rise going unconnected.
Crate in the station loft; notebooks to the state office in 1936 and the college library in 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Petition of January 1925.
Frick, three sittings and two in the weigh room are present, but the bolded dates (17 March - 4 May 1925) are not.
Water (manager), theft (bookkeeper) and the 1908 wet-hay findings were all heard; 'No cause established'.
Section A never mentions the four-book exhibit list or Strawn's 1923 notebook as an exhibit.
Dismissal and '$3,800 without admission' are present, but not 'charged to the station account'.
Section A never says the award was a fifth of $19,000 or that it was charged to the gain account.
Granddaughter, State Agricultural College at Farland, Vaught. 'Great-niece' appears only as a corrected report.
Story 8 traces the weigh book, Strawn's 1923 notebook, the Alder Corners figures and the ledgers converging on Ivy.
February 1958, station loft, nine survived.
States the mean delivery as 16.27 c.c. (planted NT-1), not 16.72.
Section A says 'about 5 percent' but never '3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood, 0.19 short'. The 16.27 in the same passage conflicts with it.
76,000 lb and the station gain appear in the story 7 quote, but not the 40,000,000 lb or $19,000; all four elements are required.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; 33 years after dismissal, 24 after death; crate in the loft 35 years.
Granddaughter, derived through Duncan.
Second cousins, correctly derived. Never raises full vs half siblings (A08) and says the chain has 'no ambiguity'; no definite full/half claim, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose, and the significance: Gideon wrote Article VII, and Selby enforced it and accused the patrons. (Manager from 1911 deducted separately.)

Never says the question cannot be settled. Treats Duncan's denial as 'carries more weight' and gives the 'resolution' as no relationship, weighting a family denial the key says is not a record. Scored as an assertion of A01.
Uses 16.27 and gets 92.44%, 7.56% short; key is 0.95.
True average 3.90, deficit 0.29; key is 3.80 / 0.19.
States 76,000 lb, quoted rather than derived, and the period is muddled; the number matches.
$19,000; $3,800; 20 percent, one fifth. $19,600 appears only as the Chronicle's figure.
True test 3.90, 7,800 lb, 960 lb owed; key is 3.60 / 7,200 / 360.
1,440,000 lb (arithmetic error); key is 1,444,000.
1,364,000 lb (sign reversed), with an alternative of about 1,560,000; key is 1,520,000.
Names both denominators but gives 5.28% of credited; key is 5.26%.
Itemised sum of $77.93. '$77.39' appears only as a hedged variant.
72 pipettes is right, but the shortfall is given as 1.33 c.c. (from 16.27), with 0.88 only as an alternative.
Gives '26 years' and '21-26 years', and explains the difference by the 1902 complaints; key is 26 years 6 weeks vs 25 full years, part years excluded.
A02: attributes 1.1M to a memory and calls it 'unverified in any document... unreliable'. No verdict in its own voice, so an abstention.
Variable: the measuring glass.
Tester, herds, pasture, season and machinery held constant.
3.80 for nine weeks, then back to the former 3.61 level when the station's glass returned.
Cause is in the glass, not the milk, cows, land or men; limit: the interval does not measure the size of the error.
Only the 1911 interval is a keyed valid reason. The others are ledger uniformity (not heaviness) and heavy-cream testimony attributed to Sill and Oram's father. Not three valid reasons.
Argues the reasons are independent and names the 1911 interval as holding without the 1958 measurement.
A09 asserted: 'He never questioned the ledger entries in real time.'
Yes, he knew the station tested low, citing the 1919 circular.
Only two of the five: signed the ledger sheets and wrote the 1919 circular. Gives manager from 1911, not 1913. Nothing on watering at the hearing or glassware never named.
Never declares the understatement question unsettleable. It offers two possibilities without asserting either, so no deduction.
1897 vs 1898 outfit date resolved by the invoice; 76,000 vs 67,000 resolved by Bulletin 471; Bulletin 214's 0.2 vs 0.05 resolved by the bulletin itself.
NT-18: Chronicle and Falke both say great-niece; broken by Duncan's family record and Falke's correction. No other pairs identified.
A04, A06 and A10 not addressed.
Cites only Falke's open retraction, which is none of the key's on-the-page self-refutations.
Cause given as 16.27 'or' 16.72, '7-5%', true 3.90-3.80. Never derives 0.19 as 5% of 3.80, and no 1896/1924 3.80 bookends.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer.
Theft (Teague) defeated by the 1911 interval under the same tester and by heavy cream arriving, not light.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and by Alder Corners.
A07 asserted: 'Answer: No.'
A05 asserted: 'Ansel Keddie privately suspected the glass', resting on the son's account.
About 142 words.
Names essentially none of the nine record series.
Wrong headline figure '7% less milk' (the 16.27 cascade) and the 0.19 Hollow-vs-valley conflation.
Only 1958 of the six arc elements: no one part in twenty, no 1897, no 76,000/$19,000, no 1923, no names.

deductions.reason: Corruption: pipettes measuring 16.27 c.c. asserted (A story 6, C1, C4, F1)
Corruption: Strawn's circuit begun 1908 ('from 1908 forward', story 3 and F)
Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 (B3, D3)
Corruption: 1919 circular sent to eleven families (story 3, D3)
Corruption: 1908 committee sampled the whole of 1908 ('monthly through 1908', story 2)
Corruption: Bulletin 214 shown to depress butterfat by 0.2 in winter, stated as fact in story 2
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved on Duncan's denial (B4)
Gullibility A09: 'He never questioned the ledger entries in real time' (D2)
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glassware, 'Answer: No' (F)
Gullibility A05: tester 'privately suspected the glass' (F)
